title: Cumulative assessment: Days 1–6
orientation: Attempt these newly authored items without the lesson open, then use their explanations and writing rubrics to plan targeted revision. Earlier phase concepts remain available for review. This is a self-study assessment; there is no time-to-expertise or examination-mark guarantee.

items.prompt: In The officer will record the interview, record is a:
items.why: Record is a plain-form lexical verb after will and takes the interview as its object.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses an object complement?
options: The board considered the proposal workable.
items.why: Workable describes the object the proposal; it is an object complement, not a second object.

items.prompt: Two ____ were found near the river. Use the ordinary plural of child.
items.why: Children is the irregular plural of child; it does not need a second plural ending.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses research in its ordinary general uncountable sense?
options: Their three researchs support the claim.
Their many research supports the claim.
Their an research supports the claim.
items.why: The ordinary general sense is uncountable and takes singular agreement. Specialised count uses need their own context.

items.prompt: The speaker has not identified any particular doctor: We need ____ doctor urgently.
items.why: A doctor introduces an unspecified singular countable person. Doctor begins with a consonant sound.

items.prompt: Which wording normally suggests that a small but useful number of chairs remain?
options: A few chairs remain; we can lend you two.
Few chairs remain, so none can be supplied.
items.why: A few has a positive small-quantity interpretation. Few tends to emphasise scarcity; little and much do not quantify ordinary plural countable chairs.

items.prompt: The coordinator spoke to Sam and ____.
items.why: The coordinated phrase is the complement of to, so objective me is appropriate; removing Sam and makes the case relationship clear.

items.prompt: Which statement about the pronoun in Someone left their umbrella is defensible?
options: Their forces the next verb to be singular.
items.why: Singular they and its possessive their can refer to an unspecified person. Someone still takes singular finite agreement in its own clause.

items.prompt: The clerk does not ____ the original files.
items.why: Do-support carries tense and agreement; the following lexical verb is plain-form destroy.

items.prompt: In The town grew quiet, quiet is:
items.why: Grew is linking in this context; the adjective quiet describes the subject town.

items.prompt: The account is still open and the period extends to now: We ____ three payments so far this month.
items.why: Present-perfect have received connects the completed payments with the current open period. We selects have.

items.prompt: Our usual office is closed. We ____ in a temporary room this week.
items.why: Present progressive are working presents this explicitly temporary arrangement; the auxiliary agrees with we.

items.prompt: Analyse The museum gave the school a replica and explain the two object functions.
items.model: The museum is subject; the school is indirect object/recipient; a replica is direct object/theme.
rubric: Do not call both objects subject complements.
alternatives: A different response is valid if it preserves the specified meaning and satisfies every stated structural constraint.

items.prompt: Explain a normal contrast between I have read the report and I have been reading the report.
items.model: The simple perfect can present the reading as completed; the progressive highlights the activity and does not by itself guarantee completion.
rubric: Explain the viewpoint rather than treating both as identical.
Allow context to supply completion or continuation.
alternatives: A different response is valid if it preserves the specified meaning and satisfies every stated structural constraint.

items.prompt: Describe a current study or workplace project in 90–120 words. Include a routine, a temporary activity, a completed result and an activity extending towards now. Identify the four forms after the passage.
items.model:
Our reading group meets every Wednesday in the college library. We usually choose one short article and discuss the writer’s main argument. This week we are preparing a joint presentation instead, so each member is checking a different source. We have already agreed on the central question and collected the most relevant references. I have been comparing two accounts of the same event since Monday. Their conclusions differ, and I still need to examine the evidence behind them. The librarian helps us locate older material when a source is unavailable online. Our shared notes record uncertainties as well as useful findings.

Analysis: meets/choose describe routines; are preparing presents a temporary activity; have agreed presents a completed result; have been comparing presents an activity continuing towards now.
rubric: Write 90–120 words of connected prose, excluding the grammatical annotation.
Include every requested construction and identify its form and meaning.
Check reference, tense, clause boundaries and meaning; this is self-review, not an external grade.
alternatives: A different response is valid if it preserves the specified meaning and satisfies every stated structural constraint.
